subject: Game Theory
title: R&D as Commitment
description: A quick, practical guide to R&D as Commitment.

hook.text: Intel spends $15 billion a year on R&D. This isn't just investment—it's a strategic signal.

buildup.text: Massive R&D spending tells rivals: 'We'll always have the next chip. Don't bother competing.'

discovery.text: The commitment changes the game. Potential competitors divert resources elsewhere, knowing they can't match.

twist.text: But overcommitment to one direction creates blind spots. Nokia's R&D couldn't save it from the iPhone.

climax.text: R&D spending is strategic when it deters entry. It's wasteful when directed at the wrong technology.

punchline.text: Spend to deter, not just to invent.

quiz.question: How does R&D spending serve as strategy beyond innovation?
options: It signals commitment and deters competitors
